programs.title: NC Medicaid
programs.rationale: The questions the DHB-5200 health-coverage application itself asks, as reviewed in the full-form mapping round (kb/forms/dhb-5200.json): who is applying and for what coverage, household composition, income with its conditional branches, shelter and cost expenses, photo ID, date of birth, citizenship/immigration status, disability, veteran status, and how mail and messages reach the person. Deliberately left out: goal_detail (a free-text navigation note the application has no field for), student_status and received_benefits_before (the printed form does not ask them) — the talk stage still covers every spec question the quick-questions stage does not capture. Added November 2026 (milestone work-requirements): the Medicaid work-requirements questions, adopted as QUESTIONS ONLY from Civilla's user-tested plain-language application insert (https://civilla.org/work/hr1/), are required because of the CMS interim final rule published June 1, 2026 (H.R. 1), work requirements effective January 1, 2027. The DHB-5200 (rev 2020) carries no such fields, so they are collected here so the person answers once; they are NOT linked to DHB-5200 registry fields, and nothing in the app determines exemption or compliance — the state decides. wr_student_enrolled (enrollment full-time or at least half-time) carries the work-requirements student path; the pre-existing student_status stays excluded as before. The screens are household-level, matching Civilla's insert: one applying member's exemption hides the reporting section for the household, and the $580 screen reads the household's captured income — the state decides how exemptions and reporting apply per person, so the app records household-level answers only and never derives a per-person exemption. Added November 2026 (HACK-130, Civilla's dedicated seasonal-work question): job_income_seasonal and job_income_seasonal_total are required so a seasonal worker's job income is captured as a last-6-months total and averaged across those 6 months deterministically by the $580 match, instead of the person being asked to average fluctuating pay themselves; the seasonal question asks whether ALL of that job work is seasonal, so mixed year-round + seasonal work stays on the per-paycheck questions.

programs.title: NC Food and Nutrition Services (SNAP)
programs.rationale: The questions the DSS-8207 Food and Nutrition Services application itself asks, as reviewed in the registry round (kb/forms/dss-8207.json, rev 10/2024): who is applying and whether an authorized representative is involved, the state and county the household applies through, household composition (the application's household chart), income from jobs, benefits, and other sources with its self-employment and prior-employer branches, the expedited-benefits screen's shelter and utility cost boxes, the living-situation and disability/age-60-or-over sections, date of birth, the optional citizenship columns, student status (the form's half-time ABAWD question), veteran status, and how mail and messages reach the person. The registry's spec_question_id links (date_of_birth, phone_contact, email_contact, housing_cost, utilities_cost, received_benefits_before, veteran_status, state) join this universe automatically. Deliberately left out: id_status and id_issue_detail (the printed form asks no photo-ID question), main_goal and best_time_to_reach (the form has no fields for them — the talk stage still covers them), and the work-requirements screen questions (the Civilla insert serves the Medicaid work requirements; the DSS-8207's own ABAWD situation boxes are form fields, not spec questions). Nothing in the app determines eligibility — SNAP is decided solely by the county DSS; the app prepares, the person reviews, signs, and submits themselves.
